text:
Predicates:
ScheduleMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Appear(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
HaveLunch(x, y) ::: x has lunch in y.
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
Customer(x) ::: x is a customer.
Company(x) ::: x is the company.
Home(x) ::: x is home.
RemoteWork(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InCountry(x, y) ::: x is in country y.
Premises:
∀x∀y (Employee(x) ∧ ScheduleMeeting(x, y) → Appear(x, Company)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (Employee(x) ∧ HaveLunch(x, Company) → ScheduleMeeting(x, Customer)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (Employee(x) → (HaveLunch(x, Company) ∨ HaveLunch(x, Home))) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (HaveLunch(x, Home) → RemoteWork(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (Employee(x) ∧ InCountry(x, y) → RemoteWork(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬RemoteWork(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ Appear(james, Company)) ∨ (¬Manager(james) ∧ ¬Appear(james, Company)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
¬HaveLunch(James, Company) ::: James does not have lunch in the company.
